short: Côte d'Ivoire has a published digital strategy for 2021-2025, now past its period, and a 2025 successor whose adoption is not known.
gaps: The Strategie nationale de transformation numerique 2025-2035 (successor) was validated in August 2025 but no adopting act is on record, so it cannot be staged above 2; its text is not shown public. The 2026-2028 ministry roadmap and the PND 2026-2030 are not national-class instruments. Reporting is claims of delivery (fibre km, services) measured against no stated target. No dated event inside the last twelve months.

short: Cameroon has a published digital plan adopted in 2016 whose period has ended, and an update in preparation, so progress is not known.
gaps: The plan's own text gives 2016-2020 (CMR-006) while the ITU repository gives 2016-2025 (CMR-003); both end before 2026. The update of the plan (Strategie numerique du Cameroun) is at diagnostic stage awaiting government approval, with no text or period. No reporting against the plan is held, and no finance fact falls inside the 36-month window.

short: DR Congo validated a national digital plan in 2019, now past its period, and a 2026 successor whose adoption is not known.
gaps: Plan National du Numerique Horizon 2025 was validated at a 2019 workshop with no cabinet act on record, so adoption is not established. Its successors, the Politique sectorielle de l'economie numerique 2026-2030 (validated 4 Aug 2026, to go to the Council of Ministers; no action plan, steering body or monitoring yet) and the PNN2 2026-2030 (drafting or announced, costed, period 2026-2030), are not adopted. Reporting is a ministry estimate of 60% completion, not measured against targets. The two successors are not reconciled.

short: Congo adopted Vision Congo Digital 2025 by decree in 2019; its successor is awaiting approval, and its action plan and monitoring are not known.
gaps: No row for a public text of Vision Congo Digital 2025; no action plan or monitoring shown, and no domestic budget line for it. The successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, is validated at ministry level but not adopted by decree; its finance is donor (World Bank) only.

short: Comoros adopted a public, costed digital strategy to 2028 in 2018; results against its targets are not known.
gaps: No row for any published report on results against the strategy's targets, so rungs 4 and 5 are not reached; no domestic budget line tied to it; no dated event in the last twelve months. The adopting act is not named.

short: Cabo Verde approved a digital economy strategy to 2030 in 2024; its public text, plan and reporting are not known.
gaps: No row for a public text of the Estratégia para a Economia Digital 2025-2030, none for its plan, reporting, body or finance. Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation (Resolução 72/2026 sets bases only; CPV-003 calls it approved, CPV-010 says it approves no strategy) and is not adopted; the 2019-2021 Agenda has ended.

short: A national digital strategy was still to be written in October 2025, but later mentions leave its status not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: DJI-001 (7 Oct 2025) records the elaboration of a national digital strategy as a challenge still open, but systems.csv shows later mentions of a Smart Nation strategy, a 'stratégie numérique' presented at WSIS 2026 and a decision to update the Smart Nation Strategy (World Bank, 10 Feb 2026), none described or dated as adopted, drafting or launched, so absence cannot be claimed as stage 1 and no rung above is set. Other national instruments (AI strategy, Digital Code, Vision 2035) are thematic, directive or development-plan and set nothing.

short: Algeria adopted its national digital transformation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in May 2025, but costs and results against its targets are not known.
gaps: No adopting act is named (approval stated by El Chaab and the High Commissioner only). Reporting is activity throughout, measured against no strategy target, so stage 4 is not reached; the plan has actions with no cost (executive plan 2027-2030 in preparation); no domestic budget line is tied to the strategy (UNDP/Japan donor support only). Earlier DZA-050 'drafting' (Aug 2024) and 'announced'/'validated' rows are superseded by the later adoption rows.

short: Egypt's Digital Egypt strategy, running from 2016, is listed as adopted in 2025, but its text, plan and recent progress are not known.
gaps: Adoption rests on the ITU repository's general listing (2025), with no adopting act, body or date, and no row shows the text public; no delivery plan, no domestic budget line, and reporting is activity only (EGY-005, Nov 2024). A second instrument, the National strategy for building a fully digital state, was announced for approval by the Supreme Council on 13 Mar 2024 with no approval recorded; it is not the instrument staged. Nothing on record in the last twelve months.

short: Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, according to a June 2026 legal-status page; whether any is in preparation is not known.
gaps: The only statement of absence is a third-party legal-status page (Levellers, reviewed 8 June 2026), not an Eritrean government source. Systems.csv holds only ministry-plan, thematic and sector-ict instruments (HSSDP III, IGIF action plan, ICT in Education policy, Communications Proclamation 1998), none a national digital strategy, so nothing stands in the way of stage 1 but nothing lifts it either.

short: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 in November 2025, but its public text and period are not known.
gaps: No text: public row is held for Digital Ethiopia 2030, and no period is stated for it. The only public-text row (ETH-003) is for the predecessor Digital Ethiopia 2025 (period to 2025, ended; superseded 20 December 2025). No domestic finance line is tied to the 2030 strategy (ETH-002 is the predecessor's), and reporting is activity only, so stage 3 needs a public text and stage 4 needs published results.

short: Gabon's national digital plan covered 2020 to 2025 and has ended; a successor is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: The strategy's period ended in 2025, before 2026, and no successor is on record in a dated evidence row. The nearest candidates are systems.csv lines only: a 'stratégie de l'économie numérique' said by UNESCO to be under preparation in June 2025, and later references to a 'stratégie nationale de transformation numérique' with no act, content or period; none is described as a national successor, so stage 2 for lapsed-with-successor is not reached. Adoption rests on a general ITU repository listing naming no act; no text, plan or reporting row is held. The donor finance row (GAB-005, AfDB, Nov 2020) is outside the 36-month window.

short: Ghana's Digital Economy Policy and Strategy was adopted in 2024 with a 2028 target; whether any progress report exists is not known.
gaps: No progress report against the policy's own actions is held, and no body is named as mandated. A research report dated 2025-10-08 (GHA-001) still calls the policy not final, but it rests on 2022 survey data and is dated only by publication, so it does not outweigh two 2024 rows saying approved and adopted. A successor, the National Digital Transformation and Emerging Technology Strategy, was only begun in April 2025 (GHA-010) and is not adopted. Stage 4 needs reporting published within three years, and the cap needs a mandated body and a domestic budget line.

short: Guinea's 2023-2027 digital strategy is public and costed, with a lead ministry named, but whether any progress report exists is not known.
gaps: No implementation or results report is held, so reporting is not established. Standing is read as adopted because the ministry published the text (version 1.2, 11 June 2024) and no source calls it a draft, but no adopting act is named; GIN-001 says validated and GIN-010 says its elaboration was still under way in December 2024. The period reads 2027 in the title and 2026 in one article (GIN-011). Also held: the 2016-2020 predecessor, ended, and a World Bank mention of a planned national digital economy policy and strategy (GIN-009) that names no document. Stage 4 needs published reporting within three years.

short: The Gambia's Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is published and reported adopted in 2024; its delivery plan and any progress report are not known.
gaps: The master plan has no governance, delivery-plan or reporting row of its own; the plan and finance rows (GMB-006, GMB-007) belong to the Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028. That strategy is only validated (May 2024, GMB-004, GMB-013, GMB-015) with no accessible text (GMB-014), so it would stand at stage 2. Adoption of the master plan rests on a third-party report that names the government and Sept 2024 but no act; it is dated 2023-2033 in some sources. Stage 4 needs a costed or actioned plan and published reporting.

short: Guinea-Bissau adopted a 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy by decree in March 2025, with a public text, but any report on results is not known.
gaps: No published report against the strategy's targets is held, so stage 4 is not reached; the plan states actions with dates but no cost. No mandated body is stated. Earlier statements that no national strategy existed (2022-2023, GNB-018 to GNB-020) and the January 2025 launch and drafting rows are superseded by the gazetted decree; a conflicting 2026-04 Fintech Times line (GNB-003) is a general remark that does not outweigh the decree.

short: Equatorial Guinea's national digital economy strategy was in drafting with World Bank support in September 2026, and its adoption and published text are not known.
gaps: No adopting act, period, plan or reporting is held, and no text is published; the strategy was still being completed and validated on 2026-09-02. The earlier ADIGE digital agenda (2019-2025, a ministry plan) has no evidence rows here; no body or finance is stated.

short: Kenya published a costed national digital master plan for 2022-2032, but any published report against its targets is not known.
gaps: No published report against the plan's targets is held, so stage 4 is not reached. Body (ICT Authority, KEN-035, 2022) and donor finance (KEN-023, 2023-03-31) are dated before the 36-month window and are not carried; no domestic budget line is stated. No dated event in the last twelve months. The Digital Economy Blueprint 2019 (open period) is the predecessor.

short: Liberia has a National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, adopted per a March 2026 policy, with a costed plan, but results against its targets are not known.
gaps: No progress report against the strategy's targets is held, so stage 4 is not reached; no adopting act or date is named (adoption rests on the ministry's National Data Governance Policy saying Liberia 'has adopted' it, March 2026). Other national-class rows are the same instrument; the Digital Liberia ministry plan, Executive Order 163 and the NDMI are noted classes.

short: Libya's Prime Minister approved a government digital transformation strategy in April 2025, to 2030, but its approved text is not known.
gaps: The text held (LBY-007) is the December 2022 proposal, marked as a proposal on its cover; the strategy as approved in April 2025 is not held, and whether it differs is not established. No budget or mandated-body row is held for the instrument, and no results report. The rows under the name National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030 (LBY-001, LBY-002, LBY-003) are the same strategy's later activity claims and an earlier drafting row. Stage 3 needs the approved text public.

short: Lesotho's digital transformation strategy to 2030 was approved in February 2025 and is published, but its action plan and results are not known.
gaps: No adopting act or date is named for the strategy (approval is the finance minister's statement of 19 February 2025 and a World Bank document); the only plan row says its action plan was still to be developed in 2024-2025, and no later one is held. No body, finance or results row is held for the strategy itself. The National Digital Policy 2024-2035 (LSO-004 to LSO-007, LSO-010) is a second adopted national instrument, with a mandated body, actions and no cost, also stage 3; the strategy is the newer adoption and the one the study names.

short: Morocco has Maroc Digital 2030, listed as adopted in 2025, with MAD 11 billion for 2024 to 2026, but a public text is not known.
gaps: No row holds the Maroc Digital 2030 text as public, and the ITU listing names no adopting act or date; other rows call it launched or announced. Predecessor Maroc Numeric 2013 / Maroc Digital 2020 (ended 2020) and the 2020 ADD orientations note (to 2025) are not in force. Stage 3 needs a public text; reporting is only activity (MAR-004), so stage 4 is further off.

short: Madagascar has the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028, presented in 2024 with a USD 800 million estimate, but its adoption and public text are not known.
gaps: No source uses adopted, approved, enacted or gazetted for the Plan Strategique Numerique 2023-2028, and no row holds its text as public; no reporting against it. A separate national digital roadmap (announced, from the Digital Readiness Assessment) is only prospective. Stage 3 needs a source's word of adoption and a public text.

short: Mali has a digital economy policy validated in 2024 with an action plan to 2029, but its adoption is not known.
gaps: PNDEN was validated at a workshop on 24 October 2024 and no source states adoption; no public text row. Periods conflict: 2021-2034 (MLI-007), action plan 2025-2029 (MLI-010), 2024-2028 (MLI-013, earlier). Predecessor Mali Numerique 2020 (ended 2020; draft-marked text, 27.30% execution rate) is not in force. Stage 3 needs adoption and a public text.

short: In 2019 Mozambique approved a national information society plan running to 2028, but its delivery plan and published results are not known.
gaps: No delivery plan is stated for this instrument in the rows (its Plano Operacional is approved with it but no row gives actions or cost), and no published report against its targets is held; one older INTIC report (MOZ-031) gives its period as 2019-2023 against 2019-2028 in the resolution. The National Digital Transformation Strategy is still in drafting (launched 12 Feb 2026, its operational plan not costed, work deprioritised by the World Bank in 2025-26) and would replace it.

short: Mauritania approved a costed national digital agenda for 2022 to 2025 that has now ended, and results against its targets are not known.
gaps: The agenda's mandated body (Haut Conseil du Numerique, MRT-020, MRT-023) is dated 2022 and 2020, outside the 36-month governance window, and its funding is donor-backed with no domestic budget line. No report against the agenda's own targets is held, only claims of activity. The successor, Agenda National de la Transformation Numerique 2030, was opened for preparation on 4 Dec 2025 (a consultant was contracted in July 2025) and has no adoption or text.

short: Mauritius launched a national digital transformation blueprint for 2025 to 2029 in 2025, and its cost and results against targets are not known.
gaps: No source names an adopting act; adoption is read from the published text with no source calling it a draft, and from the presidential launch of 26 May 2025. The plan states no cost, and reporting is claims of activity (about 84 projects) measured against no target, so stage 4 is out of reach. One launch-day report (MUS-013) said the content was not yet unveiled; the full text was published on the MITCI site the next day. The earlier Digital Mauritius 2030 Strategic Plan (2018, to 2030) is also on record and is superseded by the Blueprint.

short: Malawi has a National Digitalization Policy for 2023 to 2028, approved by Cabinet, but whether its text is public is not known.
gaps: No row says the National Digitalization Policy text is public, and its scope is not described by any source. A National Digital Economy Strategy 2023-2028 is also held (adopted per MWI-025, awaiting Cabinet in MWI-028; may be the same document). A National Digital Transformation Strategy is in validation (draft, February 2026; MWI-004, 006, 008) with a proposed council and donor finance only. No delivery plan or reporting on record.

short: Namibia launched its National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 in August 2025 with a public text; any delivery plan or progress report is not known.
gaps: No source names an adopting act or body; adopted rests on the published text (mict.gov.na, NAM-007) that no source calls a draft. Period is 2025-2029 in most rows and 2025-2028 in NAM-006, 013-016. No delivery plan, cost or progress report on record, and no finance row; a domestic budget line is also missing. No other national instrument held.

short: Niger's digital development policy for 2026 to 2035 was validated in March 2026 and awaits an approving decree; its text is not known.
gaps: The Politique nationale de developpement du numerique 2026-2035 is complete but awaiting its approving decree (June 2026); no adoption on record and no text row. The earlier Politique nationale du numerique 2021-2030 was drafted in 2020 and never adopted (NER-014 says no policy in March 2025). Stage 3 needs adoption and a public text. No cost, reporting, body or finance rows.

short: Nigeria has a ten-year digital economy strategy unveiled in 2019, but results against its targets and its funding are not known.
gaps: Reporting is activity only (statements of progress, no results against the strategy's targets), so stage 4 is out of reach; the plan states no cost, and no finance fact falls inside the 36 months. A 2025 repository gives the time frame as '2020 - ongoing' against the stated 2030 end, not a conflict for the rung. No other national instrument is held.

short: Rwanda's Smart Rwanda plan, issued in 2015, ended in 2020, and a successor was in preparation in 2023, but its current status is not known.
gaps: No text-public row for the Smart Rwanda 2020 Master Plan and no plan or reporting row. The Digital Transformation Strategy for Rwanda (ICT Master Plan 2021-2025) is held by one row (RWA-001) giving only its period, ended before 2026; nothing shows it adopted, and nothing on its text or reporting. Whether Smart Rwanda Master Plan II (drafting, 2023-10) succeeds that plan is not stated; no later row on its status.

short: Sudan's digital transformation ministry announced a strategy in 2025, but whether it was adopted or its text published is not known.
gaps: One row: a 2026 bank tender refers to a strategy announced by the digital transformation ministry in 2025; no adopting act, text, period, plan, reporting or governance fact is held. Adoption and a public text are what stand in the way of stage 3.

short: Senegal launched its New Deal Technologique for 2025 to 2034 and published the text, but whether results are measured against its targets is not known.
gaps: No source names an adopting act; adoption rests on the government's own published text (presidence.sn), which no source calls a draft. Reporting is activity only (first-year achievements, SEN-024, SEN-030), measured against no targets; the only execution rates (SEN-062) belong to the predecessor Stratégie Sénégal Numérique 2025 (period to 2025, replaced by the New Deal, so not a successor in preparation). The body (PM-chaired GouvNum) has no named act.

short: Sierra Leone approved its National Digital Development Policy in 2021 and publishes the text, but who approved it is not known.
gaps: No act or body is named for the approval (SLE-002 says 'approved' in 2021; the policy text itself, SLE-011, only recommends approval). Governance facts for the policy (SLE-014 body:none, SLE-015 finance:not-stated) are dated 2021, outside the 36 months, so governance is empty; nothing dated in the last twelve months. Other national instruments held: National Innovation and Digital Strategy 2019-2029 (public text, standing only launched; also stage 3, older), National Digital Development Strategy 2022 (validated/drafting, no adoption or public-text row) and a draft National Digital Transformation Roadmap. Stage 4 needs a delivery plan and published results; the policy has neither.

short: Somalia launched a Digital Transformation Strategy for 2025 to 2030 after a consultation in October 2025, but whether it was adopted is not known.
gaps: No source reports adoption: the strategy was validated in consultation on 12-13 October 2025 (SOM-004, SOM-006) and then said to be 'launched' by the government on 16 October 2025 (SOM-002) with no adopting act or body named. No text is held or linked, so no public-text row exists. No governance, delivery plan, reporting or last-twelve-months fact is held. No other national instrument is on record.

short: South Sudan was still developing its digital road map and master plan in June 2024; whether it has been adopted is not known.
gaps: No adopting act, body, text, period, plan or reporting held; the last dated row is June 2024 and says the Road Map/Master Plan was still being developed. Rung 3 needs adoption and a public text. A 'South Sudan Digital Transformation Strategy' and a 'Digital Government Strategy' appear in systems.csv with no evidence rows.

short: The government of São Tomé and Príncipe had launched a national digital transformation strategy by March 2026; its adoption, text and period are not known.
gaps: The government 'has launched' the strategy per a World Bank document of 2026-03-11, with no title, act, date, body, text, period, plan or reporting; a launch alone is announced, not adopted. Rung 3 needs adoption and a public text. The 2020 Estrategia Nacional para a Governacao Digital (approved by Resolucao 35/2020, period 2020/2024) is class government, noted and not assessed.

short: Eswatini has a 2024-2028 digital strategy named in sources, but its standing, text and plan are not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: evidence.csv holds no row for this country. systems.csv names an Eswatini Digitalisation Strategy (2024-2028, 'Government in Your Hand') and a Digital Transformation Roadmap in procurement, with no evidence rows setting standing, text, period, plan or reporting.

short: In 2026 Seychelles gave two bodies the lead on its digital strategy, but its standing is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: The only row is governance (SYC-001, 2026-09-17); no row gives the strategy's standing, text, period, plan or reporting, and finance is not stated. The country also holds a 'national digital plan' and a 'digital transformation strategy' named in passing, and a National Digital Economy Action Plan of 2022 with no date or standing, none with a dated standing row.

short: Chad has a 2020 to 2030 digital transformation strategy, but its adoption and public text are not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: No row on this instrument says it was approved, adopted, launched or drafted; sources only name it as existing, with period 2020-2030, and text public is not stated, so standing is not established. The World Bank (2023) both cites the strategy and says there is no comprehensive national digital strategy (TCD-003), and recommends adopting 'Chad Digital Strategy Horizon 2030' (TCD-004, drafting), which may be the same document but is a different named instrument. Tchad Connexion 2030 (national development plan and economic strategy) is also held. Needed for stage 3: a source word of adoption and a public text; no reporting row.

short: Togo's president said in 2022 the Togo Digital 2025 strategy was adopted, but its text and its 2025 to 2030 successor's progress are not known.
gaps: No public text is held for Togo Digital 2025, no delivery plan row, and reporting is activity counts only. Governance rows (2021) are outside the 36-month window and nothing is dated in the last twelve months. Successor Togo Digital 2025-2030 is only at consultant recruitment (May 2025, TGO-011/012/013) with no later row; a Global Fund audit (TGO-002, 2025-06-04) reports no coordinated national strategy, which does not outweigh the President's dated word of adoption.

short: Tunisia's National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025 and no named successor is held, so no stage is set.
gaps: Stratégie nationale du numérique 2021-2025 ended in 2025 and no successor strategy is on record: TUN-001 gives only a 'broader national vision for 2026-2030', not a named strategy in preparation. Also holds rows for the predecessor Plan national stratégique Tunisie Digitale 2020 (extended to 2025), whose body row (TUN-008) is not carried to this instrument; no text, plan or governance rows for the 2021-2025 strategy.

short: Tanzania's Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 was launched in 2024 and is public; its cost and any report on its targets are not known.
gaps: No finance line tied to the framework; no published report against its targets (TZA-011 is activity only); plan states dated targets with no cost. A World Bank March 2023 row (TZA-022) calls the then-current strategy a draft, superseded by the 2024 launch.

short: Uganda published its Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 in 2022 with a costed plan; any report on progress is not known.
gaps: No reporting row for the Vision, and its governance rows (2022-09, UGA-019, UGA-020) fall outside the 36-month window. Also holds rows for the Digital Transformation Roadmap 2023/24-2027/28 (newer, launched 2023 by the Ministry/Government, source verbs 'developed' and 'launched', no adopting act and no public text on record, so announced only); an adoption act or published roadmap text would make it the instrument in force. The Vision's adoption rests on the read-as-adopted rule, with no approval act named.

short: South Africa has a final draft digital masterplan dated 2021, not public, with its 2020-2025 period ended; its adoption is not known.
gaps: No row says the Masterplan was approved or adopted; the only text held is the February 2021 final draft, and Economist Impact (2023) says the final version is not public. Its 2020-2025 period has ended. A Digital Economy Framework and Strategy (ZAF-004, 2023, drafting, to go to Cabinet) is the possible successor, with nothing newer. Stage 3 needs adoption, a public text and a period not ended. No governance facts held.

short: Zambia adopted a public national digital transformation strategy in 2023, running to 2027, with no cost stated; progress against its targets is not known.
gaps: No report on progress against the strategy's targets is held, so reporting is empty. The delivery plan states no cost. ZMB-005 and ZMB-007 say only 'formulated' (announced) and are outranked by ZMB-002, which says 'was adopted' without naming an act. Also on record: the National Electronic Government Plan 2023-2026 (government class, not assessed). No change on record in the last twelve months.

short: Zimbabwe began defining a national digital roadmap for 2026 to 2030 in November 2025; whether it was adopted or published is not known.
gaps: The only row on the National Digital Roadmap 2026-2030 is the November 2025 start of its formulation; no later row says it was validated or adopted, and no text, plan or reporting is held. The Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan (to 2030) has one row (ZWE-002, governance, 2019, outside the 36-month window) and none on its standing, text, plan or reporting, so it cannot be placed above stage 2 either. Stage 3 needs an adopted instrument with a row showing its text is public.

short: Clinics report on paper, and municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2025).
gaps: No row names the tiers using the system, and no count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published; the one source says facilities report on paper, undated beyond its June 2025 publication. The strategic plan is in preparation and not reported as adopted, and the 2024 domestic allocation (AGO-010) is not tied to the system by name.

short: Health centres enter their own reports into the national reporting system (2023), but no figure shows how many of them do.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of health centres keying their own reports: the newest fact on the point (BDI-007, mid-2022) publishes none, and disagrees with BDI-027 (2020), which reads 'all health centres enter their data themselves' as 100% with no numerator, denominator or date, and with BDI-016 (2019), which says 'the majority' without a figure. Nothing on clinics is dated inside the last three years; the community flag rests on one UNICEF stock application described as interfaced with DHIS2 and still in test in 2023.

short: Health zone offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system in 2022; how many clinics enter their own is not published.
gaps: No number or share of primary clinics keying their own reports is published: the 2022 yearbook says only that certain equipped facilities and community relays do (BEN-017, against BEN-016 the same year), and the one count held is a single named private clinic in Cotonou (BEN-006), which does not carry the country. Tiers rest on 2019 and digitisation on 2022, nothing below the health centre is named, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to the as-at; the domestic budget line is for the directorate's information systems and does not name SNIGS or DHIS2.

short: Clinics and hospitals reported into the national system in 2024, entered at district or facility; the share of clinics entering their own is not published.
gaps: No source gives a number or share of primary clinics, or of districts, keying their own monthly reports; the facts disagree on where data is digitised, the newest (BFA-007, 2025-01) saying facility entry is being scaled up while the 2024 yearbook (BFA-022) still gives district keying from paper as the general route and facility entry only in the districts implementing it. Finance is not stated, and no row shows a community system exchanging data with Endos-BF: community reports reach it on paper through the CSPS and the district (BFA-041).

short: All public health facilities reported into the national system in 2016-18; they report on paper (2025), and it is unclear where the figures are entered.
gaps: No admitted source names the level at which facilities' paper reports are keyed: BWA-002 establishes only that entry is not at the facility, and the one row saying district (BWA-003) is from the excluded source. The 100% figure (BWA-025, 2018) counts facilities reporting through DHIS2, not clinics entering their own data, and has no numerator or denominator; tiers and that share are dated 2018-19. Inside the 36 months no plan or finance fact is held, and nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: The national reporting system runs in all 35 districts (2025), but only 21.4% of 14 facilities checked in 2024 entered data electronically.
gaps: No fact says primary clinics enter their own reports: the 21.4% is 3 of 14 hospitals and health centres chosen for access and security in Bangui and three regions (to July 2024), not a national share, and the only tiers fact is from 2020. The plan and the donor finance are dated 2020 and 2022, outside the 36 months, and the completeness rise to 2025 is a year-dated trend, not an event placed inside the twelve months; CAF-004 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: In 2020 departmental health offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system; nothing more recent shows where reports are entered.
gaps: Every coverage fact dates from 2020 to 2022 and nothing later says where clinics' reports are keyed. The 2021 plan has DHIS 2 deployed in a few first-contact establishments (CIV-025) without saying they enter their own reports, so T3 is not held and the 2020 statement that none do stands. No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months, no dated event inside the twelve, and the community flag rests on the platform publisher's own statement in systems.csv.

short: The national system is in use countrywide with entry at the facility (2022 ministry plan), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so.
gaps: No source gives a count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 96% completeness for October to December 2025 measures reports received in DHIS2, not who keyed them. Where data is digitised is in dispute: the ministry's April 2022 plan says facility entry (the newest dated fact, and nothing on tiers or entry point is dated since), while its 2020 plan and WHO's SCORE (2018 data) put entry at district, and the 2022 plan still budgets a device per facility at 20% of users a year. Tiers are not broken down by level in any source. A DHIS2-based community system was designed and piloted in 2022, with no row showing it exchanging data with the HMIS, so community integrated is not set.

short: Health zone offices enter facilities' paper reports into the national system (2021), which covers 75.3% of all health facilities (2022).
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after 2022. The 75.3% (12,050 of 16,010 facilities, 2022) is the share of all facilities whose monthly reports are in DHIS2, not of clinics keying their own, and the source does not say who keys them; no share or count of facilities entering their own reports is published. The tiers value is from Sud-Kivu alone (COD-026), and the national table of 2020 (COD-032) names only health centres and referral hospitals. No plan dated inside the 36 months is held: PNDIS II ended in 2024. The advancing event (COD-005) is an HIV analysis dashboard inside the national DHIS2 made the primary tool in one province, not a change in where data is entered.

short: All 52 health districts enter clinics' paper reports into the national system (2024); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
gaps: No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and the PNDS says facilities report on paper; health posts (T4) are not mentioned and general hospitals (T1) were configured but not yet reporting. The 401 data collectors equipped for electronic transmission are dated only to 2025, with no tier, denominator or software named, so it is not established that the event falls inside the twelve months or that it is facility entry; WHO (COG-006) does not say whether entry is at the facility or the district.

short: The national reporting system reached all 91 public health facilities (WHO, 2025), but it is not known where their reports are entered.
gaps: No row says where DHIS2 reports are keyed: the 99% (2024), the 69 facilities (August 2024) and the 91 structures or 100% (2025) are shares of all public facilities the system reaches or that report through it, not of primary clinics entering their own data, and the only keying level on record is the region, for the predecessor GESIS in July 2021. Tiers are read from 'all public structures' only; the plan row is dated July 2021, outside the 36 months, and the 2025 extension is dated to the year, so it cannot be placed inside the twelve months.

short: The national reporting system operates in every public health facility (February 2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held: the two terms of reference say DHIS2 is in production in all structures, which is deployment, and CPV-004 says the source does not state who keys the reports. Nothing on the HMIS is dated after 2024-02, and no plan or finance is stated for it.

short: 84% of all health facilities entered their own data in June 2025; it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
gaps: Inside the 36 months no row gives a current plan naming the system or a domestic budget line: the only plan rows date from 2020 (DJI-016, DJI-020) and the only finance row is UNFPA's support for one integration (DJI-008). The 84% is of all facilities with no numerator or denominator, the tier row names the primary care level only, and nothing is dated inside the twelve months to the as-at (the 69% to 84% rise ends 2025-06-30); the 2020 tier rows (DJI-017 T2;T3, DJI-022 none) disagree with the 2025 one, which stands.

short: The ministry began training staff on the national reporting system in December 2023, starting with a team of 20; nothing yet shows it in use.
gaps: The two rows held (DZA-008, DZA-009) are governance only: a first team of 20 trained on DHIS2 in December 2023 and a digital health strategy still in draft in November 2023. Nothing says which tiers report through it, where data is keyed or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; finance is not stated, and there is no dated statement that reporting has no digital entry.

short: Births and deaths are entered at district level into the national health information system (2025); routine clinic reporting is not shown.
gaps: The one row describes the flow of birth and death notifications only, from health offices on paper to electronic processing at district level; nothing shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system, and the latest year the source cites is 2011. No tier, clinic share, governance or twelve-month fact is held.

short: Reports are entered at zone and sub-zone offices (2024); no primary clinic is shown entering its own.
gaps: No row states that any primary clinic enters its own reports, and no share or count of clinics is held outside the excluded source (ERI-001). The district reach disagrees across rows: all zobas by 2019 (ERI-011), 44% of districts in 2022 (ERI-008), zones and sub-zones in 2024 (ERI-004), and no row says in so many words that sub-zones key the clinics' paper forms. The tiers fact is from 2021; finance is not stated; the plan row (ERI-006, HSSDP III 2022-2026) is dated 2021-10, outside the 36 months, so plan:current is not carried; nothing is dated inside the twelve months.

short: Hospitals and health centres enter their own reports into the national system (2024); it is not known whether health posts do.
gaps: No share of primary clinics entering their own reports is established: the 95% figures count all health facilities using DHIS2 (ETH-021, published 2023, no counts) or 'eligible' institutions implementing it (ETH-031, over 4,000, including district hospitals and district offices), while ETH-022 and ETH-023 from the same 2023 study say health posts have no HMIS of their own and report on paper through their health centre, and systems.csv counts 17,903 health posts. These disagree, and nothing dated after 2020 says health posts enter their own data. ETH-024 is a 2025 annual completeness figure, not a dated event; eCHIS is said to synchronise with DHIS2 by one undated regional page and not to be linked by two later sources, so community integrated is not set.

short: The national system was launched in December 2024, with 122 data managers trained across 51 health departments; clinics are not shown entering their own reports.
gaps: No source gives a share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports, and none names the tiers: GAB-027 says only that DHIS2 integrates all functional public facilities, and that the clinics report on paper is stated only by the excluded source (GAB-003). Completeness figures disagree (60% to 85% at the December 2024 launch in GAB-029; 35% in 2024 and 40% in 2025 in GAB-011), and the 2025 rise carries a year only, so no dated event is placed inside the twelve months.

short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national system, and some community health posts enter their own (2024); how many is not published.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of primary clinics entering their own reports: the ministry's 2022 plan says only that 'most facilities' enter into DHIMS2 themselves, and the one survey (86 purposively chosen CHPS zones in six Northern Region districts, March 2024) both reports entry at CHPS level (GHA-009) and CHPS staff without logins or computers whose paper goes to the district (GHA-010). The only clinics figure is none of 16 facilities in 2016-2017, a sample that does not carry the country. The plan is the Ghana Health Service's digital health policy and strategy for 2023-2027 (GHA-043), which names DHIMS II and covers the as-at; the ministry's 2022-2025 plan has ended. Nothing on DHIMS2 is dated inside the twelve months. No dated event falls inside the twelve months: the newest, the end of the projects that paid for the servers, is of December 2023.

short: All levels reported into the national system in early 2026, with clinics' paper reports entered at district offices.
gaps: No share or count of health centres or health posts entering their own reports is published; the 100% completeness of Q1 2026 (GIN-009) is data transmitted, not facility entry. The sources disagree on where data is keyed: the 2021 yearbook and a 2022 project statement have some health-centre heads entering in DHIS2 (GIN-034, GIN-037), while the newer rows have paper tools keyed at the district (GIN-025) and rural centres reporting on paper (GIN-024); GIN-025 is dated only to its published year.

short: Clinics reported on paper, and regional health offices entered the figures into the national reporting system, in 2024.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and nothing is held for the twelve months to the as-at. The tiers facts disagree: the policy (GMB-016, the newest) puts DHIS2 at the regional directorates and the centre only, GMB-013 shows one secondary hospital feeding it automatically in a pilot, and GMB-025 and GMB-027 say every tier's data reaches DHIS2 without saying where it is keyed; no finance fact falls inside the 36 months.

short: Health centres' paper reports were entered into the national system at 11 health directorates (June 2023); how many clinics enter their own is not published.
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after June 2023. Clinics: the 2022 yearbook (GNB-010) counts reports, not centres keying their own, and disagrees with the 2018 pilot value (GNB-020), whose tablet entry from health areas has no later fact and no number of sites. Tiers: the 2019 presentation (GNB-017) gave T1;T2;T3 and the 2022 yearbook row speaks of health centres only. Governance: the plan fact (GNB-013, PENSIS 2022-2026) is dated 2022 and is carried because its period covers the as-at; finance is donor on the one row inside the 36 months (GNB-022, the Global Fund through UNDP), and no domestic line is stated. The October 2026 support agreement (GNB-021) is for data quality, dashboards and patient-tracking tools, not a change in where reports are entered.

short: The national reporting system was piloted in two districts, Baney and Añisok, in 2025; a planned national expansion in 2026 is not confirmed.
gaps: No source names the tiers or counts the facilities entering data in the Baney and Añisok pilot, and nothing dated after November 2025 shows the national expansion foreseen for 2026 under way. The digitised facts disagree by place: facility or district-office entry in the two pilot districts (GNQ-017, GNQ-018), paper sheets transcribed to spreadsheets by ministry staff elsewhere (GNQ-015); the plan held in the window (PNDS 2021-2025, GNQ-013) is not said to name DHIS2, and the domestic budget facts are of 2019 and 2020, outside the 36 months.

short: Facilities across the country enter their reports online into the national system (2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so themselves.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics keying their own reports is held: KEN-041's 94% (2019/20) is a reporting rate, not facility entry, and KEN-035 names no tier individually. KEN-036 (2024, entry at the facility) and KEN-024 (2016, district and national) disagree on where data is digitised; the newer stands. Finance rows are 2015 and 2016, outside the 36 months; the plan row KEN-038 is dated 2023-07, two months before the window opens, and is kept because the plan runs to June 2027. No dated event falls in the twelve months. No dated event on the reporting system falls inside the twelve months.

short: All facilities report monthly into the national system (2024), with district and county clerks entering the figures from paper forms (2022).
gaps: No national figure for clinics entering their own reports: LBR-037 finds none in 48 facilities of three counties (2022), which does not carry the country, and LBR-043 and LBR-046 publish none. Nothing on where data is keyed is dated after 2022-07; the only last-twelve-months row (LBR-008) is dated to the year 2025 and cannot be placed inside the window, and the CBIS is described as a DHIS2 sub-system while its integration with DHIS2 is still planned, so no community flag is set.

short: The national system was rolled out to 465 primary care facilities and 51 hospitals in 2023; how many clinics enter their own reports is unknown.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 465 primary facilities (LBY-025) are where DHIS2 was rolled out, with no denominator, and WHO says consistent facility reporting remains a challenge (LBY-016). Sources name hospitals and PHC facilities, not levels; a 2021 assessment (LBY-007) called DHIS2 a pilot not in routine use, against the ministry's 2021 report tabulated from DHIS2 entries (LBY-032); the 2024-2025 operational plan is not shown to run to the as-at, and the donor finance fact is dated 2023.

short: 231 facilities report HIV figures into the national system (2025); clinics entering their own data is shown only in four pilot districts, up to 2017.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of primary clinics entering their own reports: facility entry is evidenced only for the four pilot districts to June 2017 (LSO-024) and for reports automated from the eRegister (LSO-017), and how facilities without it enter theirs is not stated. Tiers and clinics have nothing dated since 2017; finance inside the 36 months is not stated (the donor rows are 2015 and 2022); the 2025 advance (LSO-003) is dated to the year only and the same year carries falling reporting rates (LSO-018, LSO-019), so no twelve-month flag is set. LSO-004 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: A national reporting system was working in every public health centre by December 2019; no figure shows how many centres enter their own reports.
gaps: The coverage facts disagree: at December 2019 the SMIPF-SC was operational in every public health centre (MAR-013, MAR-014), worded as 100% with no numerator or denominator, while the newer March 2023 baseline has an integrated system deployed at hospitals and only begun in primary centres, with no count (MAR-026, MAR-027). No source says the health centres key their own reports (MAR-015), and nothing on coverage is dated after March 2023; finance:domestic (MAR-024, 2022) falls outside the 36 months.

short: Health centres in all 114 districts report into the national system, with district offices entering their paper forms (2023).
gaps: No count or share of basic health centres keying their own monthly report: the electronic RMA is available in 10 pilot districts of 114 with no facility count (MDG-017), and the 2025 deployment of electronic registers and tablets (MDG-002) gives no count either. The donor-finance statements (MDG-014, MDG-027) predate the 36-month window, and the WHO facts on completeness, modernisation and CHRD data quality (MDG-001 to MDG-003, which disagree on direction) are dated only to 2025, so none can be placed inside the twelve months.

short: Community and referral health centres and hospitals had routine data in the national system in 2019; how many clinics enter their own is not known.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 98% of September 2019 (MLI-016) is DHIS2 deployed in community health centres, with no numerator, denominator or statement of who keys, and facility entry is evidenced only for four sub-districts of Mopti in 2018 and, uncounted, for SNISI terminals at CSCom and CSRéf. Tiers and coverage are not dated since 2019; finance is not stated inside 36 months (the donor-dependence fact is of February 2021) and no dated event falls in the last twelve months; MLI-005 and MLI-006 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: District health offices entered facilities' monthly paper forms into the national system in 2019; nothing more recent is held.
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after 2019, and nothing says which tiers use SIS-MA or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; the clinics value rests on a 2016-17 sample of 16 facilities in four districts. MOZ-016 (2019, a literature review citing a 2013 paper) gives facility-level recording and disagrees with MOZ-019 and MOZ-013, which describe district keying from paper; it names no facility entering data and is not followed. Finance is held only from 2019 (MOZ-017, donor), outside the 36 months, and no event is dated inside the twelve months.

short: District offices enter health posts' paper reports into the national system (2023); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 92 per cent in MRT-016 is report coverage, with no numerator or denominator, and MRT-011's 'deployed nationally' (2025) is not facility entry and disagrees with MRT-017 (2023), which has DHIS2 piloted and not scaled up. Health posts report on paper, only two hospitals are integrated (MRT-010), and the one event in the twelve months is a training workshop for district focal points (MRT-008).

short: In January 2022 the national system was used only at regional and national level, with entry by clinics still planned; nothing more recent is held.
gaps: No row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, and nothing on the HMIS is dated after January 2022: whether the decentralisation to district and primary level then planned has happened is not established, nor whether DHIS2 carries routine patients-treated reporting rather than surveillance and immunisation aggregates. Governance facts are all from January 2022, outside the 36 months, and the plan they name ran 2020-2024, so no governance value is held; the only digitised facts are a 2018 rating of no electronic aggregate entry at district level (MUS-027) and a 2020 statement on Rodrigues alone (MUS-035).

short: District offices enter paper reports from 1,266 facilities into the national system (2023); how many health centres enter their own is not published.
gaps: No count or share of health centres entering their own reports is published (MWI-040, MWI-050, MWI-061). The sources disagree on where data is keyed: the ministry's 2023 report says DHIS2 Mobile allows direct entry by all health centres (MWI-048, MWI-049), while the later-dated study (MWI-043) and the August 2023 survey (MWI-022) find paper forms keyed at the district office. The only plan on record is a 2019 finding with no period (MWI-039), so no plan is held at the as-at.

short: Clinics report on paper, and district officers enter their monthly forms into the national reporting system (2026 study).
gaps: No row sets the tiers in use, and no share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: the minister's count of over 90 clinics reached by data collection (NAM-020, May 2025) has no total and names no system, and the newer NAM-004 and NAM-005 (March 2026) have district entry from paper and clinics on paper, so the newer stands; NAM-015 (2025-09) has four of 20 respondents saying primary facilities upload some data. On the plan, the managers' statement that no health information systems policy exists (NAM-008, published March 2026) stands against the National Digital Health Policy 2026-2036 launched in February 2026 (NAM-018), whose period covers the as-at. The only event inside the twelve months is that launch (NAM-019), not a change in where reports are entered.

short: A 2023 ministry guide has health centres enter their monthly reports into the national system; no figure shows how many do.
gaps: No count or share of integrated health centres keying their own reports into DHIS2 is held: the 2023 guide prescribes facility entry and does not measure it, and the only figures are 2021 completeness and timeliness of reports transmitted. Nothing on finance is dated inside the 36 months (the donor financing row is 2019), nothing is dated inside the last twelve months, and no community system is shown exchanging data with the SNIS.

short: 91.5% of all health facilities reported into the national system in June 2025, with local government offices entering the figures from paper.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: NGA-028 (2025-06, valued facility) only encourages states to deploy devices for direct reporting and gives no count, and it disagrees with NGA-030, NGA-032 and NGA-033, which have paper forms keyed at the LGA office. The only clinic figure is 0 of 16 sampled facilities in 2016-2017 (NGA-025), which does not carry the country; no dated event is held for the last twelve months, and the domestic commitment in NGA-010 is not broken down to DHIS2.

short: Every health facility enters its own reports (audit to 2023); it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
gaps: No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months to the as-at: the only plan fact (RWA-020, plan:none) is dated 2021 and no row states finance, so the cap holds. The 100% is a rollout statement with no numerator, resting on 13 facility visits; whether the 1,250 health posts key their own reports is not established, the newest tier fact (RWA-024, 2024-06) names no T4, and reporting completeness is held only undated (RWA-011). Nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: Local health offices entered facilities' reports into the system in 144 of 189 localities in 2020; nothing since April 2023 shows where data is entered.
gaps: Every coverage fact dates from 2018 to 2022, before the conflict of April 2023; nothing since says where data is keyed, which localities still enter it or whether any facility enters its own, and the ministry's 56 per cent reporting coverage at the end of 2025 has no numerator or denominator. On tiers the 2021 figure for selected hospitals (SDN-023) disagrees with the 2020 and 2018 statements that DHIS2 was not in hospitals or facilities (SDN-027, SDN-035), and it does not say the hospitals key their own reports.

short: The national system is used at every level, with figures entered from the district upwards (2021); how many clinics enter their own is unknown.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and no coverage fact is dated after 2021. The facts disagree on where data is keyed: the ministry's 2021 plan (SEN-025, newest) runs DHIS2 from the districts up, while SEN-057 (2021) and SEN-020 (2018, four districts) describe entry at health posts. The regressing fact inside the twelve months (SEN-035) carries its document's date, not an event's, and the finance in SEN-036 was not yet approved.

short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national reporting system (2020 procedure, 2023 assessment).
gaps: No fact says a primary clinic keys its own reports: the 96% of SLE-010, SLE-032 and SLE-039 is DHIS2 deployed in facilities surveyed, with tracker applications joined in, and SLE-041 puts T3 and T4 under that deployment only. The January 2023 facts disagree on where data is digitised, at the facility in hospitals (SLE-042) and at the district (SLE-043); the district stands for the clinics, on the April 2020 procedure (SLE-048), and nothing dated since says whether the 2020 plan to move entry to community health centres took effect. Finance is held only for 2022, outside the 36 months, and no event is held for the last twelve months.

short: District offices enter paper reports into the national system (2022), and 111 primary facilities report digitally (2025); their share of all clinics is unknown.
gaps: No denominator of primary clinics is held for the 111 facilities that produce their DHIS2 reports digitally, and no share of facilities entering their own data is published; the 2026 commentary calls implementation uneven without a figure. The facts disagree on where data is digitised (district from paper in September 2022, facility in the 111 RAAD sites by 2025) and on tiers (T4 primary health care units counted in 2022, no facility-type breakdown in the 2023 bulletin). The August 2025 UNICEF and HISP agreement falls outside the twelve months, so advancing rests on one NGO training in Bosaso in February 2026; the plan is read as current on the 2022-2026 and 2022-2027 periods, the five-year strategy's own period not being given.

short: The ministry says 30% of all health facilities entered their own reports into the national system in 2025, without giving the numbers behind it.
gaps: The 30% is a share of all health facilities with no numerator or denominator, and the tier of the facilities keying their own reports is not stated; the two 2025 facts on where data is keyed disagree (SSD-015 facility, SSD-016 centralised at a level it does not name), and SSD-011 says the PHCC and PHCU vouchers are configured, not where they are keyed. On the plan, the HSSP 2023-2027 targets for DHIS2 (SSD-019) stand against a February 2025 self-assessment that lists an HIS strategic plan as still to be established (SSD-008).

short: The national reporting system was introduced in all districts in 2024-2025; who uses it and where reports are entered is not yet known.
gaps: No admissible row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, where the data is keyed or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; the only rows on those three aspects (STP-001, STP-002) come from the excluded source. Finance is held only as donor at September 2022 (STP-012), outside the 36 months, and the advancing event (STP-006) is dated to the 2024-2025 biennium with no month, so it falls in the twelve months only on the year-end reading.

short: Hospitals and maternity units record births and deaths digitally (2022), and the national reporting system was introduced in 2024; clinic reporting is not yet shown.
gaps: No row says which tiers enter routine aggregate reports, where clinics' reports are keyed, or how many primary clinics enter their own; the one digitised fact (2022) is hospitals and maternities recording births and deaths, and it disagrees with the 2019 profile's statement of no electronic aggregation (SWZ-032). No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months; the only plan fact is from 2019.

short: The 2022 health plan describes data capture as mainly paper-based, with digital work stalled; nothing shows digital reporting, so no stage is set.
gaps: No row gives the tiers reporting digitally or the primary clinics entering their own reports. The one coverage fact (SYC-004) says capture is primarily paper-based and the eHIS work begun in 2020 has stalled, which is neither a dated statement of no digital entry at any level nor a contracted rollout; it carries the plan's published year, not a date of its own. The ministry's ownership is dated 2022, outside the 36 months, and finance is not stated.

short: District offices enter health centres' monthly paper reports into the national system (Gavi audit, 2024); how many centres enter their own is not known.
gaps: No source gives a share or count of health centres entering their own reports; the only facility-level statement of none is one district in 2018 (TCD-027), which does not carry the country. Tiers disagree: TCD-019 (2023) has hospitals on DHIS2 with a slow migration, TCD-028 (2018) has health centres and district hospitals reporting on paper. Finance is donor on a 2021 fact outside the 36 months, so not stated inside the window; plan:current rests on PNDS 4 2022-2030 (TCD-022), since the 2025 strategy does not name the system.

short: 96.5% of all health facilities entered complete reports into the national system in 2021, the ministry says; there is no separate figure for primary clinics.
gaps: The share is for 2021, printed as a rate without its counts, covers all facilities and not primary clinics alone, and nothing newer is held; WHO's annual report gives 89.2% for the same year (TGO-021). TGO-026 records no coordinated digital health strategy across the systems while the PNDS monitoring plan 2023-2027 (TGO-031) names DHIS2 and runs past the as-at; no domestic budget line is stated, and community entry into DHIS2 is a procedure requirement, not an observed count.

short: Nothing held describes routine health reporting; a national health information system was named in 2021 with no sign of use, so no stage is set.
gaps: The country has no evidence row on HMIS: nothing is held on routine aggregate reporting, at any tier. systems.csv names a 'système d'information sanitaire national unifié' being put in place in 2021, unclassified and with no fact behind it.

short: Clinics report on paper, and council offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2024).
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: TZA-040 and TZA-043 say some facilities enter directly with no figure, the only clinics row (TZA-017, none) is a 2017 sample of 16 facilities and does not carry the country, and TZA-037 (facility, over 75% of 27 sampled facilities, no dispensaries) disagrees with TZA-023 (council-level entry for 11,805 facilities) for 2024. Tiers rest on a 2019 fact; finance is not stated inside 36 months (TZA-012, donor, is 2022); HSSP V, the plan TZA-035 cites, ran to June 2026 by TZA-011 and no successor period is given; the advancing event (TZA-022) is Zanzibar's ZHMIS on a proxy date. The Zanzibar validation workshop of 1 October 2025 has passed out of the twelve months, and no later dated event is held.

short: Every level reported into the national system in 2023/24, but in 2026 a mid-level health centre carried its report to the district office.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: the ministry says only that decentralising entry to facilities continued (UGA-042), and facility entry is established by census only for HC IVs and hospitals (UGA-019, UGA-020). The newest fact (UGA-007, August 2026) has many Health Centre IIIs without computers and one carrying its report to the district, which disagrees with the facility-entry rows. Finance is not stated, and the 58 to 98 per cent DHIS2 reporting rate behind the advancing flag (UGA-012) has no stated measure or denominator.

short: The national system is used at facility, district, provincial and national level (July 2026); no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
gaps: No national share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the only figure (ZAF-053, share:100%) is one province, Eastern Cape, for April 2017 to March 2020, and does not carry the country. No plan fact falls in the 36 months: the 2019-2024 strategy (ZAF-038) has ended and the plan:none statement (ZAF-036) is dated 2021.

short: District offices enter paper reports into the national system each month, with a few facilities entering directly (April 2024).
gaps: No count or share of facilities entering their own reports: Gavi's audit (April 2024) says only that 'a few' report directly, and the 99% completeness figure for 2024 does not say where data are keyed. The tier fact dates from 2019 interviews and nothing dated falls in the last twelve months; systems.csv shows a community package sending data into 'national health information systems' without naming the HMIS, so community integrated is not set.

short: All levels of the health system report on paper, and district offices enter the figures into the national system (2023).
gaps: No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is held: the newest clinics fact (ZWE-028, 2022) has facilities on paper, keyed at the district. ZWE-022 (2025) disagrees on where data is digitised, giving facility-level flow into DHIS2, but for Impilo facilities only and without saying how the rest report. No plan is current at the as-at (the 2021-2025 strategy has ended) and nothing is dated inside the last twelve months.

short: One hospital was testing a prototype electronic record for maternity care in 2019, entered after the event; nothing is known since.
gaps: The only admissible EMR evidence is from 2019: a prototype obstetric record under test at one hospital in Lubango, keyed retrospectively, and paper records at two Luanda TB facilities (AGO-015). Nothing is dated since, so whether the prototype still runs, which tiers hold an EMR, any primary clinic use, and governance inside the 36 months are all not established; AGO-005 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: 41 of 71 hospitals kept electronic patient records and six health centres were piloting them in 2023; records are not shown to be shared.
gaps: The newest clinics fact (BDI-035, count:460) is a commitment under the February 2026 memorandum, not a count achieved, and sets nothing; the last count achieved is six pilot health centres in 2023, against more than 1,000 first-level facilities. The newest authorities fact, pilot (MWI-003, 2026-06), is a two-district test of registry updating and not a measure of the connection. The systems facts of 2026 (MWI-001, MWI-002) do not say over what connection councils work; on the government network the stated use is internet (MWI-006), slow and unreliable, with government email still awaited. MWI-020 (2022-09) reads none for the IFMIS network and is older than MWI-005.

short: In 2007 one local authority of two surveyed gave some staff e-mail; how many are connected is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: The only evidence is a 2007 survey in which one unnamed local authority of two installs e-mail for some of its staff. It does not say whether that authority is outside the capital, gives no count or share of local authorities connected, and nothing is held since 2007, on governance or on the last twelve months.

short: Broadband was reported extended to 266 communes in 2026; the total of communes and what their offices do over it are not known.
gaps: No total of communes is given beside the 266, and that fact names communes, not their offices; the fact naming the mairies (NER-001) is a reception ceremony with no number and no use stated. The civil status register is operational in 102 communes (NER-009, NER-010, the newer count) but is not said to be reached online, so it sets neither the count nor `systems` use; no use over the connection is named.

short: 510 local government administration offices were counted on broadband in December 2025; how many offices there are, and what they do online, is not known.
gaps: The 510 is a count of local government administration offices with no total of offices and no number of local governments, unchanged from July 2025 to 17 December 2025; where the offices are, who provides or pays for the connections and what is done over them are not stated. The 96% of 13 November 2025 (NGA-031) names local government areas on a health ministry platform and not the office, and its source states no institutional connection, so it disagrees with the count and sets nothing; the DHIS2 entry at LGA offices (NGA-032, NGA-033) is dated 2024 and 2021, names no connection and gives no number. On owner the rows disagree: ministry as implementing agency at 24 July 2026, a majority-private company, not yet incorporated, in the August and September 2026 rows; no domestic budget line is stated.

short: District offices worked in the national civil registration system in 2024 and 2025; how many of the districts are connected is not known.
gaps: No source gives a share or a count of district offices connected, and none says in its own words who provides or pays for a district office's connection: the only explicit statement is the 2012 instruction (RWA-026), which prescribes and reports no office as connected, so `institutional` rests on district offices working in national systems. The government network linking districts is a plan (RWA-011), cells are reported without internet (RWA-006, RWA-008) but are sub-offices, and no dated event on district offices falls in the twelve months.

short: A 2022 meeting recommended fibre for localities that ask; whether any locality office is connected is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: No coverage fact is held: no source puts a locality office on a connection, names its use or counts the localities connected. SDN-001 is from the excluded compilation and sets nothing; SDN-002 is a meeting's recommendation of 22 November 2022 with no locality reported connected, and it falls outside the 36-month governance window.

short: By June 2026, 400 civil-status centres run by communes were linked to the national register; the share of communes connected is not known.
gaps: No share of communes connected is established: the 400 interconnected centres (235 in service in August 2025) are civil-status centres counted without a total of centres or of communes, and the ANEC director general said on 27 April 2026 that in some centres the circuit was never completed and elsewhere it is very slow (SEN-007 disagrees with SEN-004 and SEN-040). The communal land offices had no connection and no SIFCOM in November 2025 (SEN-019, SEN-044; the 24.7% is communes covered by that project, not connected), the Bignona town hall is one office with no system named, and the Starlink licence suspension of 7 September 2026 (SEN-003, coded regressing) is not said to have cut any office's link; who pays for the centres' links after the donor programme closed is not stated.

short: All 21 councils had internet and a national accounting system live in early 2026, the finance ministry says; who pays afterwards is not known.
gaps: The Ministry of Finance's report gives no rural share, states transactions processed live only for Freetown City Council, and counts 21 councils in one place and 22 in another. The internet contract was shown completed on 18 November 2025 with no count of councils served, and no source says who pays for the service afterwards; no domestic budget line is stated. The 2023 finding of personal modems in seven councils is superseded by the 2026 facts, not contradicted by a later one.

short: A 2022 report says finance systems are implemented in all municipalities; how their offices are connected is not known.
gaps: No row states how any municipal office is connected, or that municipal staff work in the finance systems at their own offices; no count or total of municipalities is given. Nothing is dated inside the 36 or 12 months to the as-at, and the 2019-2024 policy's period has ended, so governance and the last twelve months hold nothing.

short: One county office of eleven assessed had its own satellite link in 2021; how many of the country's counties are connected is not known.
gaps: The only evidence is one assessment of eleven of the country's local governments in late 2021: one county office, Maban, has a satellite terminal and ten have none (SSD-002 disagrees with SSD-001 on that count, office by office), and the report's own recommendations section omits Maban. No country total, no use named, who pays for the terminal not stated, and nothing on governance or the last twelve months.

short: Whether any district council office is connected is not known as at 2026, so no stage is set.
gaps: Nothing held names the institutions on the government network or puts a district council on it; the digital governance strategy is held cut off before its network chapter.

short: One town council, Ezulwini, reported its own office internet line in the year to March 2024; how many councils are connected is not known.
gaps: No source gives a share or a total: one urban council outside the capital, Ezulwini, reports its own office internet line (year to March 2024), and Mbabane, the capital's council, pays for internet (year to March 2023). No Tinkhundla centre is reported connected; the newest authorities facts (SWZ-006, SWZ-010, count:38) are a planned target for a 2027 rollout and SWZ-005 gives none connected under that project, so they set nothing and disagree with the councils' count only in subject. No national or shared system is named as worked in over the connection.

short: All 27 listed district administrations had a government email address in 2025; how their offices are connected is not known.
